title: Augmented Dickey Fuller regression on a stationary series
narrative: A stationary first order autoregression with coefficient 0.55 and an intercept in the test regression. The augmented Dickey Fuller statistic is the t ratio on the lagged level, and the whole point of specifying the regression explicitly, rather than calling a library routine, is that implementations disagree about how many observations to keep and where the trend term starts. Here the sample runs from observation lags plus two to the end, which leaves T minus lags minus one usable rows on both sides.

tolerance.rationale: Both sides read identical CSV bytes and solve the same normal equations in IEEE 754 double precision, so the only admissible difference is accumulated rounding from a different factorisation order. That is bounded well below 1e-9 relative on a well conditioned design; anything larger is a definitional disagreement, not noise.

key_overrides.rationale: P-values span thirty orders of magnitude, so a fixed absolute floor would make small ones untestable. A purely relative budget of 1e-5 absorbs the amplification of coefficient rounding through the tail integral while still failing a one part in a thousand perturbation. The 1e-300 floor only handles underflow to zero.
